chains.title: Speculative ESR1-to-PELI2 regulatory chain
chains.element: Unverified regulatory element at the variant

links.claim: This is an unsupported candidate model: it hypothesizes that ESR1 binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref C. No QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, and no ESR1 occupancy at the site is reported; the evidence does not support this direction or rank ESR1 above related TFs.
The model requires a regulatory element containing the variant, but none is demonstrated: no cCRE overlaps the site, and the nearest listed cCRE is 1868 bp away.
PELI2 is only a candidate target based on distance; no evidence links this variant or an element at the site to PELI2.
MCF7 is the stated expression context, but the supplied evidence does not establish ESR1 occupancy or activity at this site in MCF7.
A PELI2-mediated breast-cancer effect is hypothetical; the variant has no reported GWAS Catalog association, and the supplied gene-level evidence does not establish a PELI2–breast cancer link.

predictions: If this model is correct, an allele-specific binding assay in MCF7 will show greater ESR1 binding to T than C; this distinguishes it from H2's proposed FOXA1/C-greater-than-T model.
If the variant affects PELI2 through this chain, perturbing ESR1 or the site will alter the allele-dependent regulatory effect; the direction of the resulting PELI2 change is not specified.
falsified_if: A suitably sensitive assay finds no ESR1 occupancy or no T-greater-than-C binding difference at the site.
ESR1 perturbation and variant editing do not affect the proposed allele-dependent regulatory effect or PELI2 expression in relevant cells.

matrix.test: Isogenic editing of C/T at the site in MCF7 followed by PELI2 expression measurement and ESR1 perturbation

outcomes.outcome: Editing does not reproducibly change PELI2 expression in an ESR1-dependent manner.
Editing changes PELI2 expression, and the effect depends on ESR1; the expression-change direction is not specified.
No ESR1-dependent PELI2 effect; a FOXA1-dependent effect would remain possible.

next_experiment: Run allele-specific ESR1 CUT&RUN in MCF7, first confirming the cell line's genotype at the site. It is the most direct, relatively low-burden test of the proposed H1 binding step against the null; a positive result would support ESR1 occupancy but would not by itself establish an allele-specific regulatory effect, the PELI2 target, or a breast-cancer link.
